claims.text: Machine-learning algorithms can identify optimal alloy compositions.
Machine-learning-identified compositions can concurrently improve strength and ductility in metallic materials.
Existing metallic alloys have known strength and ductility properties.
Machine-learning algorithms can analyze the performance of different alloy compositions.
Machine-learning algorithms can predict the performance of different alloy compositions.
Data on prior alloy compositions and their mechanical properties are available for model training.
The identified compositions will produce an associated alloy composition and microstructure.
Machine-learning models can find correlations between alloy composition and mechanical properties in large datasets.
Composition–property correlations enable prediction of new alloy compositions.
The predicted new compositions can enhance both strength and ductility.
The method will identify new alloy compositions with improved strength and ductility relative to existing materials.
Current metallic alloys have limited concurrent strength and ductility improvements.
The proposed approach is limited to metallic materials.
The machine-learning approach depends on sufficient training data.
The effectiveness of composition identification depends on the quality and quantity of the training data.
Failure to obtain statistically significant improvements in both strength and ductility relative to traditional-alloy controls would falsify the hypothesis.
